newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE boosts Australia cotton for 96/97 and 97/98.
newsitem.headline: ABARE boosts Australia cotton for 96/97 and 97/98.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has further increased its estimate of Australia's 1996/97 (July/June) cotton crop and its forecast for the 1997/98 crop.
With harvesting of the current crop nearing completion, ABARE said on Tuesday it estimated Australia's 1996/97 production at 2.7 million 500-pound bales, or 607,000 tonnes.
This eclipses the previous record of 2.2 million bales, set in 1991/92, and is up from ABARE's previous forecast of 606,000 tonnes in its Australian Crop Report of June 3.

ABARE, the Australian government's main commodities forecaster, also forecast an Australian 1997/98 cotton crop of 608,000 tonnes, slightly ahead of the 607,000 tonne forecast earlier this month. "Abundant water and ideal weather conditions at both the beginning and end of the season have contributed to a forecast record Australian crop for 1996/97," ABARE said.
About 30,000 hectares of transgenic cotton was planted in Australia's first transgenic cotton crop in 1996, representing about eight percent of the total Australian planting, it said.
The National Registration Authority is expected to restrict the planting of transgenic cotton to 25 percent of total area of 418,000 hectares in 1997/98, ABARE said.
Despite a recent dry spell, the main irrigation dams serving cotton growing regions were at high levels, the agency said.
This, combined with continuing favourable returns to cotton, suggested that the area planted to irrigated cotton in 1997/98 would be slightly larger than the 1996/97 area, it said.
However, if recently forecast drier than average conditions in 1997 eventuate, production of dryland cotton could be expected to be constrained, ABARE said.
After an increase in the volume of exports in 1996/97 to 493,000 tonnes from 311,000 tonnes the year before, exports are expected to rise further to 529,000 tonnes in 1997/98, it said.
The value of exports in 1997/98 was forecast at A$1.07 billion, up from A$1.05 billion in 1996/97 and A$762 million in 1995/96.
